messages:
srinivas: FYI — noticed a cluster of outboard BMCs in eu-west-2 with dual-NIC failover stuck in 'backup' after the BIOS microcode push 00:45 UTC. PXE/provisioning is failing for those racks, GPUs sitting in 'awaiting-image' and backlog growing.
alex: gah. any visible pattern? model, hw rev, or vendor? :eyes:
marie: quick scan shows they're all on vendor rev 3.2.1 and bootrom 1.14. BMC logs include repeated entries:
marie: ```
SEL: NIC_LINK_CHANGE: eth0 -> DOWN
SEL: NIC_LINK_CHANGE: eth1 -> UP
BMC: failover_state=BACKUP pinned_by=bios_pinflip
``` 
jamie: pinned_by=bios_pinflip? that's new wording. could BIOS be flipping NIC priority bits on reboot? :thinking_face:
leo: ran ipmitool on one node:
leo: ```
ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.2.5.12 -U admin -P **** lan print 1
  Set in progress         : Set Complete
  MAC Address             : 52:54:00:ab:cd:ef
  IP Address Source       : DHCP Address
  Default Gateway IP      : 10.2.0.1
  Backup Gateway Enabled  : Yes
  Failover Priority       : 0x02 (secondary)
```
leo: failover priority set to secondary on both ports, so BMC never promotes primary after BIOS writes NVRAM.
srinivas: confirm also that secure-boot bit toggled to OFF on ~8 hosts. not sure if related but likely NVRAM corruption on boot flags.
jamie: ops-bot triggered 3 alerts: devops/provisioning queue > 120, rack eu-west-2-a degraded :fire:
ops-bot: Alert: provisioning_queue > 120 (eu-west-2-a). Affected nodes: 8. Severity: high.
oncall: Can we hot-fix the NVRAM instead of fleet rollback? what's the runbook say?
marie: runbook suggests ipmitool raw to set LAN priority and clear SEL tag but warns about persistent BIOS writes that will re-flip on next update. excerpt:
marie: ```
# set primary priority
ipmitool lan set 1 pvid 1
ipmitool lan set 1 defgw ipaddr 10.2.0.1
# clear SEL event (careful: audit)
ipmitool sel clear
```
leo: tested on one canary: set priority to 1, power-cycled via BMC, node came up and PXE resumed. BUT after reapplying BIOS from the push image it flipped again.
samira: capacity note — provisioning backlog causing us to hold ~96 GPUs in reserve longer; projected extra spend ~ $4k/day if we keep dedicated pools warm. we should consider pausing rollout until root cause identified.
alex: agree. pause the BIOS rollout across all regions and mark current job aborted.
jamie: already paused global rollout 00:58 UTC (canary group halted). logging in deployment system: job-id 7863 paused by jamie.
srinivas: next steps I propose:
- pause rollout globally (done)
- triage 6 canaries, replicate fix that leo did and capture exact ipmitool steps
- investigate BIOS change that writes NVRAM NIC priority bits (vendor followup)
- temporary automation to enforce BMC lan priority after deploy until vendor patch
srinivas: assigning: leo + marie to run canary triage, jamie to coordinate rollback/pause, samira to model cost impact, alex to own vendor escalation.
leo: starting triage now. will post outputs. ping me if you need a hot-fix script.
marie: created a short ephemeral playbook in ops-runbooks: https://runbooks.internal/oob/dual-nic-pinflip (internal)
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0372 "oob dual-nic failover - eu-west-2". Priority P1. Linked to provisioning alerts.
oncall: Good. full rollback of BIOS image across affected nodes will be scheduled if vendor can't confirm a patch within 6 hours. keep posting status here.
srinivas: thanks all. tagging @alex @jamie @leo @marie for updates. :thumbsup:
alex: quick note — let's also snapshot BMC NVRAM before any wipe. use `ipmitool fru print 0` and `ipmitool mc info` as part of triage.
leo: snapshot saved to s3://infra-debug/euw2/5167777777/nvram-dump-01.bin
samira: I'll prepare a short cost brief and options (pause vs rollback vs temporary routing rule) and drop it in #finance-infra.
marie: one more gotcha — a subset have secure-boot toggled OFF after the flip; need to capture for compliance. adding to triage checklist.
srinivas: update expected in ~30m after canary run. if things look bad we'll kick rollback earlier.
